GC column, HYDRODEX BETA-3P, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

Therefore, this phase shows a distinct selectivity for polar organic compounds as well as for molecules containing electron systems (e.g., analytes with double bonds). Cyanopropyl HPLC columns can be run in the RP mode using aqueous-organic eluent mixtures as well as in the NP mode, e.g., with hexane as mobile phase.

products.name: GC column, HYDRODEX GAMMA-DiMOM, 50 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, LIPODEX A, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, HYDRODEX BETA-6TBDM, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). products.name: GC column, LIPODEX G, 50 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, LIPODEX C, 50 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, HYDRODEX GAMMA-TBDAc, 50 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, LIPODEX B, 50 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, HYDRODEX BETA-PM, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

In contrast to chemical single parameter analysis, luminous bacteria tests allow an evaluation of the overall toxicity of a sample. The test method is widely used in environmental analysis, particularly for the investigation of wastewater, industrial effluents, eluates from soils or sediments, and for monitoring systems in water supply networks. The international standard DIN EN ISO 11348 regulates the performance of these tests, which are relevant for regulatory analyses in environmental agencies and wastewater analysis. It serves as an internationally recognized basis for quick and easy toxicity measurement for water and wastewater samples.

products.name: GC column, LIPODEX B, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

In contrast to chemical single parameter analysis, luminous bacteria tests allow an evaluation of the over-all-toxicity of a sample. The test method is widely used in environmental analysis, particularly for the investigation of wastewater, industrial effluents, eluates from soils or sediments, and for monitoring systems in water supply networks. The international standard DIN EN ISO 11348 regulates the performance of these tests, which are relevant for regulatory analyses in environmental agencies and wastewater analysis. It serves as an internationally recognized basis for quick and easy toxicity measurement for water and wastewater samples.

products.name: GC column, HYDRODEX BETA-6TBDM, 10 m L, 0.10 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description: Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, LIPODEX A, 50 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, LIPODEX E, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, LIPODEX D, 50 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, HYDRODEX BETA-6TBDE, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, HYDRODEX BETA-TBDAc, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. HYDRODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective derivatization of the hydroxyl groups leads to phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Due to the high melting point of the HYDRODEX phases they are diluted with polysiloxanes. Important advantage of cyclodextrin phases - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: GC column, LIPODEX C, 25 m L, 0.25 mm ID, proprietary df
products.short_description:
Capillary columns for GC enantiomer separation. LIPODEX cyclodextrin phases are made of cyclic oligosaccharides consisting of six (α-cyclodextrin), seven (β-cyclodextrin) or eight (γ-cyclodextrin) glucose units bonded through α-1,4-linkages. Regioselective alkylation and/or acylation of the hydroxyl groups leads to lipophilic phases with varying enantioselectivity, which are well suited for chiral analyses. Important advantage - many compounds can be analyzed without derivatization (however, for certain substances enantioselectivity can be favorably influenced by formation of derivatives). A large number of separations have been achieved, however, it is not possible to make a general prediction, which phase could solve a given separation task. Even for compounds with small structural differences or within homologous series the enantiodifferentiation can be quite different.

products.name: EC HPLC column (analytical), NUCLEOSIL 100-5 CN-RP, 5 m, 250x4.6 mm
products.short_description: The cyanopropyl phase is able to generate a clearly recognizable different retention behavior compared to purely alkyl-functionalized surface modifications. The polarity can be classified as intermediate based on multiple retention mechanisms such as dipole-dipole, -, and also hydrophobic interactions. Therefore, CN phases show a distinct selectivity for polar organic compounds as well as for molecules containing -electron systems (e.g., analytes with double bonds). This HPLC phase can be run in the RP mode using aqueous-organic eluent mixtures as well as in the NP mode, e.g., with hexane as mobile phase. This HPLC column is packed with CN modification, based on the original NUCLEOSIL silica gel. It is one of the first spherical silicas for HPLC and was originally developed by MACHEREY-NAGEL in 1974. It is exclusively manufactured in Germany and is still one of the most used HPLC silicas in quality control around the globe. Are you interested in real-world applications for this product? products.name: BioFix Lumi luminous bacteria, liquid-dried, 10 tubes for 200 tests
products.short_description: Liquid-dried BioFix luminous bacteria tests use bio luminescence to determine bio toxicity in accordance to ISO 11348‑2. In contrast to chemical single parameter analysis, luminous bacteria tests allow an evaluation of the over-all-toxicity of a sample. The test method is widely used in environmental analysis, particularly for the investigation of wastewater, industrial effluents, eluates from soils or sediments, and for monitoring systems in water supply networks. The international standard DIN EN ISO 11348 regulates the performance of these tests, which are relevant for regulatory analyses in environmental agencies and wastewater analysis. It serves as an internationally recognized basis for quick and easy toxicity measurement for water and wastewater samples.

products.short_description: Silica-based phase for HPLC enantiomer separation. Principle interaction modes - charge-transfer interactions, hydrogen bonds, dipole-dipole interactions and steric effects. For control of the optical purity of a substance, the two columns NUCLEOSIL CHIRAL-2 and NUCLEOSIL CHIRAL-3 allow to select conditions such that the minor enantiomer, which is present as an impurity, is eluted before the main peak. Thus, overlapping peaks are avoided. This makes an exact quantification of the impurity much easier. Based on the original NUCLEOSIL silica gel. It is one of the first spherical silicas for HPLC and was originally developed by MACHEREY-NAGEL in 1974.
